name: Ready For Robots robot taxonomy
purpose: Closed vocabulary for classifying robots. Extraction must choose ONLY from these values. Anything that does not fit goes in unclassified_notes and is logged, never invented. Buyer opportunities are indexed with the same industries list so matching is a join, not a semantic guess.
pipeline: 2. products: one record per robot product (multi-product sites get several records); set offering_type
3. functions: what the robot is designed for (pick 1-3)
4. industries: where it is sold (pick all that apply)
5. classification: form (pick 1) + primary_class (pick 1, the index shelf)

offering_type.robot_product: Company sells or leases a physical robot
offering_type.robotics_as_a_service: Company deploys and operates robots, charging by hour/output/contract
offering_type.autonomy_software: Company sells autonomy that runs on other makers' machines
offering_type.developer_tooling: SDKs, simulation, or platforms for building robots; not a deployable product
offering_type.mixed_equipment_maker: Conventional equipment maker with an autonomous product line

functions.delivery_transport: Moves items or materials from A to B
functions.food_beverage_prep: Cooks, assembles, portions, or makes food or drinks
functions.picking_packing_palletizing: Picks, packs, sorts, loads/unloads, palletizes, handles totes/cases
functions.machine_tending_assembly: Loads machines, assembles, welds, screws, finishes parts
functions.inspection: Scans, measures, or monitors assets, shelves, or infrastructure
functions.construction_task: Layout, rebar, finishing, installation, or material work on jobsites
functions.agricultural_task: Weeding, harvest assist, hauling, spraying on farms
functions.customer_interaction: Greets, guides, advertises, or converses with people
functions.general_purpose: Marketed as able to do many tasks without a defined primary one
functions.surgical_assistance: Assists or performs surgical procedures (e.g., surgical robots in operating rooms)

industries._definition: Industry means the industry of the organization that buys and operates the robot. It is not the building type, the project type, or the industry of that organization's customers. A construction robot used on a hospital project is construction. A warehouse robot doing pharma logistics is warehouse_distribution or 3pl. Keys starting with '_' are documentation, not values.
industries.retail_store: Retail stores, big box, specialty retail
industries.restaurant: Full-service and casual restaurants, cafes, ghost/delivery kitchens, including the bars inside them
industries.stadium_venue: Stadiums, arenas, theme parks, event venues
industries.senior_living: Senior living, long-term care, assisted living
industries.food_manufacturing: Food production plants, meal kits, co-packers
industries.energy_utilities: Power generation, oil and gas, utilities, solar/wind, mining
industries.bar_nightclub: Standalone bars, lounges and nightclubs (counts as restaurant via industry_parents)
industries.surgery_center: Ambulatory surgery centers and outpatient surgical facilities
industries.automotive_dealership: Car and truck dealerships, including service and parts (fixed-ops) departments
industries.k12_school: Primary and secondary schools and school districts
industries.transportation_transit: Transit agencies, rail and bus operators, fleet and mobility operators
industries.facility_services: Contract cleaning, food service and facility management companies
industries.residential_consumer: Homes and individual consumers. Classification only: never a buyer opportunity in RFR

form.humanoid: Human-shaped body, arms and legs or torso
form.amr_mobile_robot: Wheeled autonomous mobile robot without a manipulator
form.robotic_arm_cobot: Fixed-base arm or cobot, including dual-arm stations
form.autonomous_vehicle_equipment: Autonomous tractor, implement, sidewalk vehicle, or other vehicle-class machine
form.retrofit_kit_autonomy_software: Kit or software that makes existing equipment autonomous
form.portable_stationary_unit: Positioned by people, operates in place (e.g., UV tower)

primary_class.food_robotics: Kitchen, beverage, and food production robots
primary_class.retail: Retail robots: shelf scanning, in-store service, inventory
primary_class.service_robot: Guest/customer-facing service in hospitality, retail, healthcare

record_fields_per_product.functions: 1-3 of functions, each with confidence 0-1 and evidence snippet
record_fields_per_product.industries: list of industries, each with confidence and evidence
record_fields_per_product.form: one of form, with confidence and evidence
record_fields_per_product.primary_class: one of primary_class, with confidence and evidence
record_fields_per_product.unclassified_notes: anything that did not fit the lists; logged for taxonomy review

industry_parents._note: A child industry also counts as its parent for scoring answer keys and for pilot-industry groups. Keys starting with '_' are documentation.

changelog.change: Added industries bar_nightclub, surgery_center, automotive_dealership, k12_school, transportation_transit, residential_consumer; restaurant no longer includes bars; added function surgical_assistance; added industry_parents. Approved by Bob. Takes effect AFTER the hold-out v2 run, which stays on v1.1. Restaurants include their bars (Bob); bar_nightclub = standalone bars/lounges/nightclubs.
Added industry facility_services (contract cleaning, food service and facility management companies), in pilot group 8. Approved by Bob.
